clue.text: 15,18 I would say, vocalise about the top harshly and unmusically?

blocks.note: to vocalise is to utter words
surface padding that echoes the top in 15, setting up the cross-reference
harshly means in a rough way
taken as written
music without notes is no music at all

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to singing coarsely and tunelessly about the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 15,18 is OFF THE TOP OF MY HEAD, which both means an impromptu remark and puns on 'about the top'. 'Unmusically' is the joke: a speaker working without notes is unscripted, not tuneless.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something off the top of your head means giving a rough, unprepared answer, as a speaker would without a script.

clue.text: Energy, energy, energy - that's how to deal with jealousy

indicators.note: dealing cards scatters them into a new order, so the preceding letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy, twice

explanation.surface: A pep talk: the cure for envy is bursts of vigorous activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used once in full and twice as its symbol E.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eye is a name for envy, from Shakespeare's green-eyed monster describing possessive resentment.

clue.text: Opera singer and Pole go to bed

blocks.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A soprano and a Polish man retire for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a nationality; it is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low couch or base-type bed without a headboard, common in British bedrooms.

clue.text: See 10
Bangle for social worker that eats up deer

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
eating takes something inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: ants are social insects and workers in the colony
an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A bracelet bought for a caseworker who consumes venison.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker is not a caseworker but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An anklet is an ornamental ring worn round the ankle, a bangle for the leg rather than the wrist.

clue.text: Honorary clerks give way to breathe under water

definitions.note: describes the device's purpose rather than naming it

indicators.note: giving way means collapsing, so the letters fall apart into a new order

blocks.note: Hon. is the standard abbreviation for honorary
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unpaid office staff stand aside so that a diver can breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A schnorkel is a tube that lets a swimmer or submarine take in air while submerged.

clue.text: Bend raised at lamppost

blocks.note: first meaning: a sharp angle in a road or golf hole
second meaning, read cryptically: what a male animal lifts against a street light

explanation.surface: Something crooked is lifted at a street light.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half pictures a dog cocking its leg against a lamppost.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp angle in a road or fairway, and literally the limb a hound lifts.

clue.text: See 1
Fruit of the body, about one millimetre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part wraps round the others

blocks.note: a body can mean a person, as in somebody
I is the Roman numeral one
mm is the abbreviation for millimetre

explanation.surface: A biological phrase, fruit of the body, measured to the millimetre.
explanation.definitionFit: A persimmon is an orange tomato-like fruit from a tree of the ebony family.

clue.text: Flower: vulgar old hairdresser's about to have one for a quid

blocks.clueFragment: vulgar old hairdresser's about to have one for a quid
blocks.note: surface reading: a coarse old-fashioned barber is about to take a pound for a trim

blocks.clueFragment: vulgar old hairdresser's about to have one for a quid
blocks.note: setter's reading: an old coin worth a fraction of a pound, and the chin tuft a barber shapes, each name one word of the flower

explanation.surface: A crude old barber is about to take a quid for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose, whimsical Araucaria clue: an old crown coin was a quarter of a quid, the crown is the top of a head a barber cuts, and an imperial is the pointed chin tuft named after Napoleon III.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown imperial is a tall fritillary with a ring of hanging orange bells beneath a tuft of leaves.

clue.text: It's mean to say how old someone is

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
a person's age

explanation.surface: It is unkind to state someone's age out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as unkind but is the statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the average, the total divided by the count of values.

clue.text: Territorial rule additionally kept by barrier being put back

indicators.note: putting something back turns it round, so the word runs right to left
something kept is held inside, so one word sits within another

blocks.note: a wall is a barrier
and means in addition

explanation.surface: A regulation about borders kept in place by a rebuilt fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Land law is the branch of legal rules governing ownership and use of property in ground.

clue.text: Particular people going together

blocks.note: first meaning: a single detail or article in a list
second meaning: a couple in a romantic relationship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is used as a noun, as in 'in every particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A separate point in a list is an item, and colloquially a dating couple is called an item.

clue.text: Entry on one side is hereditary privilege

blocks.note: birth is one's entry into the world
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: Admission from one flank is a privilege handed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is an entitlement someone has simply from the family they are born into.

clue.text: My immediate comment is: "Away with my 10!"

blocks.note: off means away
10 is the crown, the top of the head

explanation.surface: Someone's first reaction is to cry 'Off with my crown!' like a deposed king.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase runs on into 18 down to make OFF THE TOP OF MY HEAD. 10 refers back to the crown of the flower clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something off the top of your head means giving an instant reply without preparation.

clue.text: Very happy to be coming back - be sensible and pull round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word wraps the other
coming back means returning, so the whole is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to lug is to drag or pull
being sensible of something means being able to feel it

explanation.surface: Delighted to return, a sensible traveller lugs a case round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' is in its old sense of aware through the senses, not wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful describes someone full of glee, a state of merry high spirits.

clue.text: Draw game with Venetian artist

blocks.note: a draw is a tied result
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A drawn match played alongside a painter from Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century painter of ceilings and frescoes from Venice.

clue.text: 24 telling time by alarm-clocks

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
alarm clocks rouse sleepers

explanation.surface: Clothing that tells the hour by bedside alarms.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is GARMENT, so the definition is a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are an article of clothing covering each leg separately, so they are one kind of garment.

clue.text: See 15

definitions.note: the clue sits at 15 down; this light completes its phrase

blocks.note: a cross-reference: these letters finish the phrase whose wordplay is at 15, where 'my 10' is read through the crown

explanation.walkthrough: This light completes 15 down's phrase OFF THE TOP OF MY HEAD; its clue and wordplay are given there, where 'my 10' is the top of my head.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the 15 down light it forms the idiom for an impromptu remark made without preparation.

clue.text: Dispatch to Austin, to the far post

indicators.note: to dispatch is to finish off, so the words are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A posting instruction: send this to Austin, at the remote office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like a verb of sending mail, matching 'post', but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstation is a remote branch or post far from headquarters, especially in the colonies or outback.

clue.text: Begin to become

blocks.note: first meaning: set to work
second meaning: change into

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means start work energetically, and also change into something else.

clue.text: Inch back into the money with Venetian artist

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction
into means put inside, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: an inch is a Scottish small island, and an ait is a small river island
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Edging back into the cash alongside a painter from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a verb of slow movement; it is the Scottish word for an islet, here swapped for its synonym ait.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiziano Vecellio, known as Titian, was the leading painter of sixteenth-century Venice.

clue.text: Produce a variant 13

indicators.note: a variant is a changed form, so the letters of the referenced entry are rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 13 across

explanation.surface: Make another version of a single article.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or send forth, such as light, sound or gas.

clue.text: Stoppage cut short by secret police

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: stasis is a stoppage or standstill

explanation.surface: A work stoppage halted early by the secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the state security service of communist East Germany.

clue.text: Man without arm could wear  one without sleeve

definitions.note: loose: a sleeveless article of clothing is one kind

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a gent is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: An armless man could only wear sleeveless clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking but means outside, so the man is wrapped round the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any item of clothing, of which a sleeveless vest or tabard is one example.

clue.text: Took a pew at church with Dr Armstrong

blocks.note: taking a pew means sitting down
CH is the abbreviation for church
an MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone sat in church next to a physician named Armstrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Armstrong' sounds like one person; the doctor is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the nickname of the jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong.

clue.text: Whatês drawn to game by Venetian artist

blocks.note: a lot is what is drawn when choosing by chance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A raffle draw becomes a game run by a painter from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a game of chance, so 'game' doubles as a second hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo Lotto was a Renaissance painter born in Venice, known for portraits and altarpieces.

clue.text: A love for speed will get you to the farthest 19s

definitions.note: a cryptic cross-reference: the remotest outposts are out in space

blocks.note: taken as written
Eros is the Greek god of love
pace means speed

explanation.surface: Passion for velocity carries you to the remotest stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is OUTSTATION, so the farthest outstations are those beyond the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerospace covers the atmosphere and the space beyond it, where the most remote stations orbit.
